summary: Wolfgang Voigt was an Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Heinrich Lüders, Bernhard Breloer, and Hans Heinrich Schaeder, and completed his PhD at Marburg under Johannes Nobel and Friedrich Heiler.

Wolfram Eberhard was a Sinology and history scholar who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and under Ferdinand Lessing. He taught at Ankara University (1937–1948) and served as professor of sociology at the University of California, Berkeley (1948–1976).
Woncheol Yun is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD at Stony Brook University. He served as Professor of Religious Studies at Seoul National University (attested 2012).

Woodford Wright Sherlock (1836–1912) was a linguistics and Indology scholar who earned an MA at Trinity College Dublin (1852). He was a lecturer in Hindustani at University College London (1884) and the University of Cambridge (1883–1912).

Woosung Huh is a philosophy and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He was attested in 2012 as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Kyung Hee University.
Wouter J. Hanegraaff is a religious studies scholar who studied at Utrecht University (~1982–1995). He held a post at the University of Amsterdam around 1999.
Wulstan Fletcher is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).

Władysław Kotwicz was a linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies scholar who studied at St. Petersburg University (~1891–1895). He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1900–1923) and the University of Lviv (~1923–1944).
Włodzimir Szajan was an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Lviv under Stefan Bołeslaw Stasiak from circa 1927 to 1935.
Xi Cao is a scholar in computational fields and Tibetology who has held posts at Minzu University of China and Tibet University.
Xianda is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a BA at the University of Kelaniya and a PhD at the University of Hong Kong by 2016, supervised by K. L. Dhammajoti.

Xianlin Ji was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt and Emil Sieg at Göttingen (PhD 1935–1945). He served as professor, vice president, and Life Professor at Peking University, and held leadership roles at CASS.

Xiaoling Wu was a Sinology and Indology scholar. He held posts at Peking University (~1937–1946), Visva-Bharati University (~1947–1949), Academia Sinica (~1953–1977), and the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1995).
Xiaoming Hou is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology who was a doctoral student and postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026).

Xiaoting Wei works in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned an MA at the National University of Singapore under Cheng Mei Ku (attested 2004) and was an Associate Lecturer at Australian National University in 2016.

Xin Huang is a Tibetology and linguistics scholar. He earned an MA from Sichuan Normal University, held professorships at Sichuan Minzu College, Sichuan Normal University, and Nanning Normal University (2023), and completed a PhD at Southwest Jiaotong University.

Xinchuan Huang was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Peking University (~1954–1958). He served as a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1977–1998).

Xinguang Ma is a scholar of religious studies, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Northwest University and held a post in the School of Chinese Language and Literature at Shanxi Normal University.

Xinru Liu is an Indology and history scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Ludo Rocher. She held posts at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences (~1985–1998) and The College of New Jersey (~1998–2018).
Xiuzhi Zeng is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies who earned a master's degree at Nanhua University under supervisor Meihua Chen (attested 2006).
